subject: Service recompense request and exec authorization for latency SLO impact
messages:
From: Daniel Hayes <daniel.hayes@bluewave.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>; Paula Kim <paula.kim@bluewave.io>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected latency spikes last week — request for service recompense

Irene / Redwood team,

We saw a sustained latency regression on your hosted inference endpoint (model: rwd-gtx-1-small) from 2026-11-18 23:40 PST through 2026-11-19 05:10 PST. 95th percentile latency jumped from ~120ms to ~850ms for our real-time patient-triage requests, and the increased tail directly impacted our live triage pipeline. We lost multiple requests to timeouts and had to fall back to local heuristics.

Attached is a short CSV with request-level timing and error rates: incident-summary-20261118.csv. We've also linked to metrics in our dashboard (see attachment link). This incident materially affected our SLA expectations; our customers flagged delayed triage notifications which has downstream business impact.

We expect Redwood to propose a remediation and a compensation path — specifically, we are requesting an account-level service credit commensurate with the disruption while you complete RCA. Please propose a formal remediation plan and a credit proposal by EOD Tuesday PST. If we cannot agree on an acceptable remediation, we will escalate to procurement/legal for the renewal conversation.

Thanks,
Daniel Hayes
CTO, BlueWave Diagnostics
phone: +1 (415) 555-0132

---
Attachment: incident-summary-20261118.csv (CSV, 78KB)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Hayes <daniel.hayes@bluewave.io>
Cc: Paula Kim <paula.kim@bluewave.io>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency spikes last week — request for service recompense

Hi Daniel — thank you for the detailed report and the CSV. I'm very sorry BlueWave experienced those latency spikes over the window you called out. That falls short of the latency SLOs we aim to deliver.

Quick notes:
- We received your logs and we've opened an internal incident ticket to capture the request traces you attached.
- Engineering has identified an unusual multi-tenant batching regression that impacted the GPU kernel selection for short sequence workloads; we are running an RCA and timeline now.

As an immediate next step I want to propose a temporary, good-faith remediation while we complete root cause and commit to a formal SLO addendum:
- Apply a one-time invoice credit of up to $25,000 to BlueWave's next billing cycle (pending exec approval).
- Provide 60 days of whitelist priority support (no-routing-downtime policy) and daily engineering syncs until mitigation is complete.

I need to escalate the credit amount for executive sign-off if we go above $25k. Can you confirm whether BlueWave would accept a $25k credit plus the support/monitoring package while we finish the RCA and a final SLO amendment? If you need a higher amount now, tell me and I will request an exec-level approval path.

I'll follow up internally and get back to you within 48 hours with an RCA timeline and a formal proposal document.

Best,
Irene Choi
Sr. Account Lead, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

Attachment: (metrics dashboard link referenced, no file attached)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:40:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: BlueWave latency incident — need exec authorization for compensation

Marissa / Rishi — forwarding BlueWave's request and my proposed interim offer (see thread below). They want a formal credit proposal by EOD Tuesday PST. Account health: high risk at renewal (Q1 2027), strategic healthcare reference.

Summary/ask:
- Incident: 2026-11-18 23:40–2026-11-19 05:10 PST; 95p latency spikes to ~850ms; attachments include request-level traces.
- Proposed interim remediation: $25,000 invoice credit applied to next invoice + 60 days of priority support + daily engineering updates.
- Business impact: potential renewal churn; procurement loop will escalate if we do not reach agreement this week.

If we want to offer >$25k to preserve the account, I'll need explicit exec authorization and a clear signature path for a one-time restitution. I drafted a short proposal (slo-credit-proposal-draft.pdf) that outlines credit mechanics (applied against the next two invoices pro-rated).

Recommend: authorize up to $25k at my level to close quickly. If you want to authorize more (up to $35k), we'll need VP signoff + a short note to include in the DocuSign addendum.

Attachments: slo-credit-proposal-draft.pdf, rca-timeline.xlsx (draft)

Thanks,
Irene
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: BlueWave latency incident — need exec authorization for compensation

Irene — thanks for the quick escalation and the draft. I reviewed the CSV traces and the initial engineering notes. This is a high-priority healthcare customer and churn risk is non-trivial given renewal timing.

Authorization guidance:
- You have authority to approve up to $25,000 in a one-time credit. Approve that immediately and close with the customer — include the 60-day priority support and the engineering sync cadence in the agreement.
- Any restitution above $25,000 requires VP-level signoff (my approval + written concurrence from VP of Sales). If they press for more, escalate to VP Sales (cc: legal if DocuSign addendum is required).
- Require the SLA addendum to include: corrective action timeline, monitoring hooks for BlueWave, and a clause for revisiting quantization/batching defaults within 90 days.

Do the $25k now. I'll prepare a short exec note and loop in legal for the DocuSign flow if we need a binding amendment.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Internal note: recommend attaching the RCA timeline and change log to the DocuSign envelope to avoid ambiguity.

Subject: Final remediation offer: BlueWave Diagnostics service credit + SLA addendum

Daniel / Paula — thank you for your patience while we completed the initial analysis. Attached is a short proposal and next steps. Per the internal approvals below, Redwood is prepared to offer the following:

1) One-time invoice credit of $25,000 applied to BlueWave's next invoice (amount will be reflected as a negative line item).
2) 60 days of priority support (daily engineering syncs for first two weeks, then biweekly) and a named escalation engineer.
3) A formal SLA addendum documenting the incident window, corrective actions, and monitoring hooks. We will include an explicit remediation timeline and an option for BlueWave to request an operational review within 90 days.

If that is acceptable, please sign the attached addendum via the DocuSign link below and we'll have Finance apply the credit to the next invoice. If you require a larger credit, let us know and we'll route for VP-level approval (this will add 24–48 hours).

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/placeholder/link/BW-SLO-2026
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/bluewave
